title: fix(setup): keep model verification out of ordinary chat events
body:
Related: #155744

## What Problem This Solves

Internal model-verification probes could appear as ordinary completed or failed chats even though their sessions are temporary.

## User Impact

Setup checks no longer publish ordinary Gateway chat or session projection. The verification call still returns success or failure, and normal user conversations remain visible. No configuration or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register the probe's existing internal-run visibility flags for its lifetime and clear them in the producer's existing cleanup path. This avoids a separate visibility wrapper, a session-name rule, or changes to Web Push filters. Equivalent local deduplication keeps the existing producer within its line limit without moving verification or execution-owner logic.

## Evidence

Current revision `9fd46910`: 16 focused setup producer and error-reporting tests pass in 20.24 seconds, including delayed success/error Gateway projection after producer cleanup (8 ms and 10 ms).

The authenticated, registered Gateway flow was rerun on a freshly built candidate at `7ab47bb5`. The current revision merges subsequent main fixes and reruns the focused suites; the full Gateway observations remain explicitly bound to `7ab47bb5`. Baseline observations are retained from the original before-repair run.

- An isolated full Gateway received authenticated `openclaw.setup.verify` requests and made real requests to a loopback model. Before the repair, successful verification exposed eight probe events including `chat.final`; a provider HTTP 400 exposed five events including `chat.error`. The same candidate flow exposed zero probe events on both paths.
- The fresh candidate preserved three visible ordinary-chat final replies, unchanged applied configuration hashes and temporary-workspace/process cleanup on success and failure. The original before/after comparison also found unchanged probe request bodies and verification responses apart from latency.
- Two consumer regressions failed before the repair, then passed. They deliver retained sequenced events to the real Gateway projector after producer cleanup, rather than asserting registration fields. The historical run of 269 Gateway projection and notification-classification tests also passed.
- The private-QA build at `7ab47bb5` completed and the registered Gateway proof exited successfully. Earlier production/test typechecks, scoped lint/format, structural ratchets and whitespace checks remain historical evidence, not fresh checks of this revision.

This proves Gateway-event projection suppression, not actual Web Push or browser-notification delivery. The reporter's original trigger and push payload were not captured, so this does not claim to reproduce that incident or close the broader report.
